newsitem.title: USA: Ford recalls Taurus, Sables, Continentals.
newsitem.headline: Ford recalls Taurus, Sables, Continentals.

text.p: Ford Motor Co announced three recalls Monday, including one affecting 445,300 1991-94 Lincoln Continentals and 1991-95 Taurus and Sable sedans, the latter two equipped with 3.8-liter engines and speed control.
Ford said in freezing temperatures the speed-control cable may freeze and not allow the engine to return to idle. The recalls affect vehicles in 23 northern states, as well as 57,300 in Canada.

Ford said it was also recalling 1992-97 Ford Crown Victoria police and taxi vehicles because the hood latch striker may either wear or become detached, causing the hood to flip open when the car is moving. About 191,000 vehicles are involved, of which 6,000 are located in Canada.

Ford said it was recalling 1,800 1996-97 Ford Contour small cars equipped with the compressed natural gas bi-fuel option to disable the option. Ford said it was possible a backfire could occur when the engine is started on compressed natural gas, causing damage to plastic components in the air-intake and air-cleaner system.
